suspend.title: Suspend {count} accounts?
suspend.body: None of them can sign in and their open sessions are closed. An access token already issued keeps working until it expires, up to an hour. Reversible at any time.

activate.title: Reactivate {count} accounts?
activate.body: They can all sign in again immediately.

delete.title: Delete {count} accounts?
delete.body: Each is soft-deleted and disappears from the default list. An account that still owns an active shop is refused, and the whole request fails with it. Restorable from the Deleted filter.

restore.title: Restore {count} accounts?
restore.body: They come back suspended, not active — reactivate them separately once you have checked them.

resetPassword.title: Send a password reset to {name}?
resetPassword.body: A one-time code goes to {identifier} — the address on the account, not one you choose. You never see it, and neither does anyone else here: the account enters the code and picks its own new password. Their current password keeps working until they do.

suspend.title: Suspend {name}?
suspend.body: They can no longer sign in and their open sessions are closed. An access token already issued keeps working until it expires, up to an hour. Reversible at any time.

activate.title: Reactivate {name}?
activate.body: They can sign in again immediately.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.body: The account is soft-deleted and disappears from the default list. It cannot be deleted while it still owns an active shop. Restorable from the Deleted filter.

restore.title: Restore {name}?

selection.selectAll: Select every shop on this page

suspend.title: Suspend {count} shops?
suspend.body: Their storefronts go offline immediately. Nothing is deleted — products, orders and settings stay as they are, and you can switch them back on at any time.

activate.title: Reactivate {count} shops?
activate.body: The active switch goes back on for each. A shop returns to the public listing only if it is approved as well.

restore.title: Restore {count} shops?
restore.body: They come back suspended, not live — switch them on separately once you have checked them.

approve.title: Approve {name}?
approve.body: The shop passes review and goes live: it joins the public listing and its storefront starts serving products and checkout. Reversible with Disapprove.

disapprove.title: Disapprove {name}?
disapprove.body: The shop leaves the public listing and its storefront stops serving — products and checkout refuse, including for anyone holding a direct link. Nothing is deleted and you can approve it again.

suspend.title: Suspend {name}?
suspend.body: The storefront goes offline immediately. Nothing is deleted — products, orders and settings stay as they are, and you can switch it back on at any time.

activate.title: Reactivate {name}?
activate.body: The active switch goes back on. The shop returns to the public listing only if it is approved as well.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.body: The shop is soft-deleted and disappears from the default list. The server refuses this while the shop still has orders that are not finished. Restorable from the Deleted filter.

restore.title: Restore {name}?
restore.body: The shop comes back suspended, not live — switch it on separately once you have checked it.

domains.title: Domains
domains.subtitle: Every address this shop answers at. Read-only: a domain is the merchant's property and its DNS lives in their registrar, so connecting, promoting and removing one happen in the vendor's own dashboard.
domains.empty: This shop answers at no address.
domains.customDisabled: Custom domains are switched off on this deployment — there is no DNS target to point one at, so the platform subdomain is the only address any shop here can have.
domains.platformNote: The platform subdomain is not a stored record: it follows the shop's handle, and its status is derived from the shop itself rather than from any DNS check — it serves only while the shop is both approved and active.
domains.platformPendingNote: So this address is pending because the shop is, not because anything needs setting up. Approve the shop or switch it back on from the shops list and it starts serving.

impact.title: What a change does
impact.body: A fee saved here applies to every shop at once. New negotiations price their minimum-margin floor against the costliest fee among a shop's payment methods, starting with the next session; negotiations already open keep the floor they started with. Negotiation outcome margins and profit analytics are worked out each time they are read, so past figures move too.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: Overrides the values in the server environment. The credentials below belong to the selected provider, and saving makes it the one the platform sends through.

source.ENVIRONMENT: from the server environment — nothing saved here is in use yet
source.UNUSABLE: saved here, but the server cannot use it

notInUse.title: This server does not use these settings.

reason.STORAGE_DRIVER_LOCAL: It stores uploads on its own disk (STORAGE_DRIVER=local), so neither the zone saved here nor the one in its environment is read. They take effect only once the server runs with STORAGE_DRIVER=bunnycdn.
reason.STORAGE_DRIVER_S3: It stores uploads in S3 (STORAGE_DRIVER=s3), so neither the zone saved here nor the one in its environment is read. They take effect only once the server runs with STORAGE_DRIVER=bunnycdn.
reason.other: The server is set up to use something else, so nothing saved here is read.

unusable.title: The {provider} settings saved here are enabled but cannot be used.
unusable.consequence: Nothing is being delivered until they are fixed.
unusable.consequenceStorage: Every upload fails until they are fixed. The server will not fall back to the storage zone in its environment: each file's address is saved with it at upload, so a fallback would point new files at the wrong zone for good.
unusable.fallback: The settings saved here are enabled but cannot be used, so the server environment is serving in their place.

reason.DECRYPTION_FAILED: The stored credentials no longer decrypt, almost always because the server's encryption key changed. Re-enter every field below and save.
reason.ENCRYPTION_KEY_MISSING: The server has no encryption key, so it cannot read any stored credentials. Set SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the server and restart it.
reason.UNKNOWN_INTEGRATION_PROVIDER: They name a provider this build of the server does not include. Choose a supported provider below and save it to replace them.
reason.other: The server could not read them. Re-enter every field below and save.

test.title: Send a test message
test.bodySms: Sends one real SMS with these stored credentials, whether or not this provider is the live one.
test.bodyEmail: Sends one real email with these stored credentials, whether or not this provider is the live one.
test.bodyMonitoring: Sends one real event to the project this DSN names, whether or not this provider is the live one. It appears in that project's Issues feed at info level, tagged as a test.
test.bodyAiChat: Sends one five-token completion to the model named above, whether or not this provider is the live one. It costs a fraction of a cent and is the only check that touches the MODEL — Verify proves the key alone, which is exactly how a retired model can take every AI feature down while the console still shows a valid credential.
test.doneAiChat: The model answered — the key and the model both work

integrations.testEventSent: Test event sent — check the project's Issues feed

plans.subtitle: What each tier sells. A capability with no row denies — a new plan grants nothing until its matrix is filled in.

plans.capabilitiesHint: Editing {code}. Each group saves on its own — capabilities you do not touch keep their current values.
plans.unsavedCount: {count} unsaved capability change(s). Each group saves on its own.
plans.limitError: "{key}": limit must be empty (unlimited) or a whole number
plans.subscribersSubtitle: Every store on a plan, live and historical. Rows marked Stripe are billed by card — their renewal date comes from Stripe, not from here.
plans.planSubscribersHint: Stores on this plan right now, and the ones that have been.
plans.subscriberNotFound: No subscription found for this store.
plans.syncHint: Subscription state comes from Stripe webhooks. If a webhook was missed, this row can be out of date — re-read it from Stripe.
plans.stripeTakeoverWarning: This store pays by card. Assigning a plan here ends its Stripe subscription — it stops being charged and the plan becomes a grant. It cannot be put back on Stripe from this console.
plans.renewBlocked: Stripe bills this subscription, so its renewal date comes from Stripe — a date set here would be a promise nothing collects on, and the next paid invoice would overwrite it. Take it over with Change plan, or leave it to renew on its own.
plans.periodLengthHint: Days. Leave empty for the subscription’s own interval. Added to {anchor}.
plans.anchorPast: today, since the period has lapsed
plans.resetHint: Sets consumption back to zero for the current window. The limit itself is unchanged — use an override for that.
plans.cancelWarning: Ends the plan immediately — the store drops to FREE and loses its capabilities now, not at the period end.
plans.cancelWarningStripe: Its Stripe subscription is cancelled too, so billing stops.
plans.overridesHint: A grant on top of the plan, for this store only. An override wins over whatever the plan says, and can expire on its own.
plans.overridesEmpty: No overrides. This store gets exactly what its plan grants.
plans.overrideLimitHint: Empty inherits the plan’s limit. Type a number to raise or lower it for this store only.
plans.overrideRemoveHint: Clearing every value removes the override rather than storing one that overrides nothing.
plans.usageHint: One row per metered call. Cost is what the platform paid a provider, not what the store was charged.

channel.title: Delivery
channel.help: Where a code is sent when the flow knows both an address and a number.
channel.scopeNote: This decides vendor signup only. OTP sign-in and password reset send to whatever the user typed — an email code cannot be delivered to a phone number they entered instead.

EMAIL.label: Email
EMAIL.help: Send the code to the email address.

SMS.label: SMS
SMS.help: Send the code to the phone number.

BOTH.label: Both
BOTH.help: Send the same code on both channels.

code.title: Code and limits
code.help: Shorter codes are easier to type and easier to guess. The limits below are what keeps that trade honest.
code.revealWarning: At {length} digits, Show code on the OTP log stops working. Reveal recomputes a live code rather than storing one, and only 4 to 6 digits can be recomputed inside a request — so support will have no way to read a code back to someone who says it never arrived.
